payload.summary: Fixed Canonical Validation 6's single root cause: DirectPostgresClient.query()/insert()/update() never JSON-decoded jsonb columns, so Task.result came back as a raw string instead of a dict, breaking TestCompleteTaskTerminalCancellation::test_late_complete_after_reconcile_cancel_is_refused both locally and in GitHub's required test-integration job. Registered an asyncpg jsonb/json type codec on the pool, reconciled its encoder with the existing _serialize_for_asyncpg pre-serialization so neither path double-encodes the other, and proved the fix against a fresh live PostgreSQL deployment.
completed_work: Added _encode_jsonb_param() and _register_jsonb_codecs() to agent-coordinator/src/db_postgres.py, and wired init=_register_jsonb_codecs into asyncpg.create_pool() inside DirectPostgresClient._get_pool(), so query()/insert()/update()/rpc() all decode jsonb/json columns to native dicts/lists via a codec keyed on the declared column type instead of runtime string-sniffing.

Reconciled the codec's encoder with _serialize_for_asyncpg's existing dict-to-JSON-string pre-serialization: _encode_jsonb_param passes an already-str value through unchanged (so a pre-serialized payload is never re-encoded into a quoted string) and only json.dumps()'s a value that was not pre-serialized (e.g. a raw list/dict reaching asyncpg directly).
Kept rpc()'s existing isinstance(result, str) decode fallback in place as harmless defense-in-depth now that the codec handles the normal path.

Added agent-coordinator/tests/test_db_factory.py::TestEncodeJsonbParam (pre-serialized strings unchanged, non-pre-serialized dict/list gets encoded, None round-trips through JSON null, non-JSON plain strings untouched), TestRegisterJsonbCodecs (registers jsonb and json with schema=pg_catalog, format=text, the module's encoder/decoder; explicit round-trip proof using the exact failing test's {'reason': 'cancelled_by_projection_reconcile'} payload shape), and TestPoolRegistersJsonbCodecInit (_get_pool() passes init=_register_jsonb_codecs to asyncpg.create_pool).

Deployed a fresh rootless Podman/PostgreSQL 18.3 stack (docker.io/paradedb/paradedb:v0.22.2, isolated network valfix6-net, port 55447), raw-initialized all 39 SQL migrations plus 999_record_schema_migrations.sh via docker-entrypoint-initdb.d; confirmed 39/39 migrations recorded.

Ran tests/integration/postgres/ against the live database: 38 passed, 6 skipped, including TestCompleteTaskTerminalCancellation::test_late_complete_after_reconcile_cancel_is_refused (previously the reproducing failure) and test_complete_still_succeeds_for_active_claimed_task, both now passing.
Ran tests/e2e/postgres/ against the same live database: 13 passed.

Ran tests/test_work_queue.py, tests/test_work_queue_invariants.py, and tests/test_db_factory.py (no tests/test_db_postgres*.py file exists in this repo; the db_postgres.py unit tests live in test_db_factory.py): 79 passed.
Tore down the Podman stack (podman rm -f valfix6-pg, podman network rm valfix6-net); confirmed zero remaining containers, networks, or listeners on port 55447.
Ran the coordinator full non-live suite (-m "not e2e and not integration"): 2,447 passed, 11 skipped, 97 deselected (up 8 from Validation 6's 2,439 — exactly the new codec unit tests).
Ran mypy src/ (77 source files, no issues) and ruff check . (all checks passed).

decisions.title: Register a pool-wide asyncpg jsonb/json type codec rather than ad hoc decoding in query() alone
decisions.rationale: Mirroring rpc()'s isinstance(result, str) fallback inside query() only fixes that one call site; insert()/update()'s RETURNING * rows have the identical defect and would still hand back JSON text for any jsonb column. A codec registered once in _get_pool() via asyncpg.create_pool(..., init=...) makes decoding uniform across every method that talks to the pool, keyed off Postgres's own declared column/return type.

decisions.title: Reconcile the codec's encoder with _serialize_for_asyncpg's existing pre-serialization instead of changing that path
decisions.rationale: _serialize_for_asyncpg (and some callers, e.g. work_queue.py's manual json.dumps for agent_requirements) already turn dicts/lists into JSON text before asyncpg sees them. A naive encoder=json.dumps codec would double-encode those already-serialized strings, storing a quoted JSON string instead of the object. _encode_jsonb_param passes through an already-str value unchanged and only serializes values that were not pre-serialized, so both paths produce identical wire text and neither can double-encode the other's output.
